Compute percent replication and QC cells from bin-level replication states

Source: R/replication_states.R
compute_rep_percent.Rd

Run two QC passes on a bins x cells replication-state matrix (states 2 = unreplicated, 4 = replicated, NA = unknown), compute the per-cell replicated fraction and return the filtered matrix with updated metadata.

Usage

compute_rep_percent(
  genobins_rep_states,
  genome_granges,
  meta_data,
  min_rep_percent = 0.001,
  max_sigma = 0.4,
  neighbor_window = 5,
  outlier_threshold = 0.2,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

genobins_rep_states

Matrix-like bins x cells replication states; row names = names(genome_granges), column names = rownames(meta_data) (same order).

genome_granges

Named GRanges with one range per row.

meta_data

A data.frame whose unique row names are cell IDs.

min_rep_percent

Minimum replicated fraction (first pass). We use 0.01.

max_sigma

Maximum sigma_chr (first pass). We use 0.3.

neighbor_window

Neighbourhood half-width for the second pass. We use 5.

outlier_threshold

Maximum fraction of local correlation outliers (second pass). We use 0.2.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallel::BiocParallelParam; chromosomes are processed in parallel in the second pass.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages. Default FALSE.

Value

A list with

genobins_rep_states_filtered

numeric matrix, all bins x cells passing both QC passes (columns ordered by increasing rep_percent), with second-pass masked chromosome blocks set to NA.

meta_data

input meta_data with added columns rep_percent, sigma_chr (numeric, all cells) and pass_qc (logical).

Details

First pass (cell level)

rep_percent = fraction of non-NA bins in state 4; sigma_chr = population SD of the per-chromosome mean states. A cell fails if rep_percent < min_rep_percent or is NA, sigma_chr > max_sigma, or at least one chromosome is entirely 2 while another is entirely 4 (has_cnv). Passing cells are ordered by increasing rep_percent.

Second pass (per chromosome)

Pairwise Pearson correlations of the cells' states on the chromosome are computed (values equal to 1 are set to NA); cells with a negative mean correlation are masked. For each cell with both states present on the chromosome, among its neighbor_window neighbours on each side in rep_percent order, the cell is masked if no neighbour correlates better with any column than it does, or if the fraction of MAD outliers (|r - median| > 3 MAD, IQR rule if MAD = 0) in its row exceeds outlier_threshold. Masked cells get NA on that chromosome; a cell masked on at least n_chromosomes - 1 chromosomes fails the second pass.

Examples

set.seed(1)
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(rep(c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3"), each = 100),
                             IRanges::IRanges(rep(seq(1, by = 1000, length.out = 100), 3),
                                              width = 1000))
names(gr) <- paste0("bin", seq_along(gr))
rp <- seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 20)
st <- sapply(rp, function(p) ifelse(rep(seq(0, 1, length.out = 100), 3) < p, 4, 2))
dimnames(st) <- list(names(gr), paste0("c", 1:20))
md <- data.frame(row.names = colnames(st), cell_id = colnames(st))
res <- compute_rep_percent(st, gr, md, min_rep_percent = 0.01, max_sigma = 0.3,
                           verbose = FALSE)
head(res$meta_data)
#>    cell_id rep_percent sigma_chr pass_qc
#> c1      c1        0.10         0    TRUE
#> c2      c2        0.15         0    TRUE
#> c3      c3        0.19         0    TRUE
#> c4      c4        0.23         0    TRUE
#> c5      c5        0.27         0    TRUE
#> c6      c6        0.31         0    TRUE
